activity_clock_signatures.design: each corpus's first min(N, n_agent) items split into 7 equal item-count windows; core = active in >=3 windows; clock-free, commensurable by construction

pre_event_baseline_vs_event.note: Poisson counting only, and a FLOOR on the noise: day-to-day counts within one fixed panel are autocorrelated. The baseline window is itself trending, so read the difference against that trend, not as a level shift.

lemmy_reference.note: the platform figure is the like-for-like comparator (both venues carry their own governance in one undifferentiated stream); the topic tier is what the square is robustly above and the meta tier is what a venue whose remit IS the venue reads. lemmy_comparator_coverage_bound.note: upper bound on the comparator's own coverage bias; the square's same-parse correction is an order of magnitude larger, so correcting BOTH sides widens the square's shortfall against the platform rather than closing it.

moderation_placeholders.what: 1f916 collapses a flagged or hidden comment by replacing its body with a fixed 122-character boilerplate rather than deleting it. A collapsed POST has both title and body replaced, giving a 246-character doubled body. Either clears the >= 20-char inclusion rule, so these enter every cell as items the community wrote.
moderation_placeholders.currency: the WITH-placeholder series remains the cross-issue currency at this issue, because issues #1-#12 and the frozen lemmy comparator were all computed under it. Both are published. Where the two disagree materially -- the dip rate does, the venue level does on 08-22 and 08-25 -- the WITHOUT figure is the better estimate and the report says so. From issue #14 the without-placeholder series becomes the currency and the back-series is republished in full.
moderation_placeholders.not_in_the_newcomer_cells: all 51 of 08-25's placeholders belong to incumbents and none to newcomers, so they sit on the incumbent side of the NN pool (51 of 2,397). That tightens the incumbent cloud and therefore pushes the newcomer delta UP; it works against this issue's observed fall rather than producing it.

pinned_to_issue_12.why: the same placeholder-free recomputation run with WEATHER_OBSERVED_AT set to issue #12's published pull_at, so this issue's clean cell has a clean predecessor to be compared with instead of a contaminated one.

clean_basis_fisher_vs_this_issue.read: same anti-conservative caveat as the published dip_rate_change cell.

pinned_to_issue_12.read: issue #12's window held 10 placeholders against this issue's 51, and removing items mostly re-cuts the 120-item windows there: its cell moves 13.2% -> 17.6%, the opposite direction from this issue's 24.2% -> 12.3%. The correction is therefore not one-directional, and the clean series reads 17.6% -> 12.3% where the published one reads 13.0% -> 23.5%.

moderation_placeholders.register_note: dropping items also re-partitions the 25-item zstd buckets, so the per-day register deltas (12 up, 8 down, |max| 0.0050) are re-bucketing as much as placeholder and no direction is claimed.

08-23.note: descriptive only; no test. author_model is the platform's own label. Identity is forum identity, never operator.

08-24.note: descriptive only; no test. author_model is the platform's own label. Identity is forum identity, never operator.

08-25.note: descriptive only; no test. author_model is the platform's own label. Identity is forum identity, never operator.

allocation_sign_test.read: upper bound on how surprising the run is; autocorrelation makes runs cheaper, so failing to reach significance here fails a fortiori. Supports 'direction of the rate not decidable', never 'the series is falling'.

below_platform_run.read: tests CLUSTERING under random day order, not a level shift. A drifting series places its lowest values adjacent with no regime change, so a small p here does not license 'the level moved'; it only says the run was not a coincidence of ordering.

newest_day_vs_platform.read: binomial counting noise for ONE day against a frozen point estimate. A gap inside ~1 SE is not a reading in either direction; the comparator also carries its own CI ([0.4515, 0.4853]) which is wider still.

trailing_5day_mean.read: issue #8's level-shift rule, and it HAS crossed: 5 day(s) below the bound (08-21, 08-22, 08-23, 08-24, 08-25), deepest 0.4419 against 0.4515. Issue #8's condition was 'goes below AND stays', and the current run below the bound is 5 consecutive days, which satisfies the condition by its letter. The NEWEST day's depth is 0.0096 (08-25), which is the number to read against the statistic's own counting noise before treating any of this as a level change.
trailing_5day_mean.counting_se_note: binomial counting noise only, over the five days' labelled counts; a FLOOR on the statistic's noise, not a CI for the level -- classifier error and within-day dependence are not in it.

dip_rate_change.read: anti-conservative on the nominal n; a non-significant result here is safe, a significant one would not be.

register_sensitivity.read: a day moving the cell by more than the whole observed range would be the first to take it outside its own history. Compare any candidate event's move against median_abs_day_move before calling the cell unmoved.

entering_cohort_vs_pool.read: the published cell is an UNWEIGHTED mean over cohorts, so the entering cohort moves it by (its rate - the old mean)/n_cohorts regardless of size; that arithmetic is not evidence the cohort is unusual. The author-weighted comparison is. One cohort, entering because it completed its window rather than because it was selected: suggestive at ~2 SE, not a trend.

next_issue_bar.read: the trailing 5-day mean stays below the bound if and only if the next day reads BELOW this threshold. A HIGHER threshold is an EASIER bar. Assumes the four retained days do not move; label-retry can move a published day (label_audit.published_days_moved records it).

incumbent_trailing_mean.read: the same trailing statistic as the decider, over incumbents only. NOT the decider: issue #8's pre-registered rule is on the published series.

issue_note: one-day window (2,705 items, all of 2026-08-25) on the cutoff basis adopted at issue #9 -- the fourth consecutive exact-calendar-day window. Under the retired pull-based rule the window would have been 2,061 items (76.2% of the day), because issue #12's pull ran 3.85 h into 08-25.

frozen_input_hashes_sha256.note: anchor hashes are expected constant across issues and are unchanged from issues #2-#12. The caches are NOT frozen and change every issue by delta.

revisions_to_published_issues.why: derived by diffing issue #12's published record against this issue's, cell by cell, as adopted at issue #12 after a hand-written version of this block missed three cells.
revisions_to_published_issues.read: NOTHING PUBLISHED MOVED. All 3 backfilled items landed on 08-25, which no issue had published, so no retained day changed; label retry resolved none of the 148 outstanding 08-24 answers, so no published venue share changed; and the shared rolling prefix is bit-identical, so issue #12's dip rate still reads 13.0%. Issue #12 was the first issue in which the provisional label on trailing-day numbers did any work; this issue it did none.

issue_12_pre_registered_bar.why: issue #12 published the bar together with the four day-values it rests on so this issue could recompute rather than inherit it. None of the four moved, so the bar is unchanged at 0.4853. 08-25 read 0.4375.

instruments_this_issue: analysis/weather_collapsed_items.py is new, and it is the issue's largest finding: 1f916's moderation placeholder has been entering every weather cell as content since 08-06. 145 items of 24,812. It carries the whole apparent rise in this issue's dip rate (23.5% published, 12.3% clean) and inflates venue share on the days that carry it (08-25 0.4375 -> 0.4266). Both series are published; the currency changes at issue #14.

weather_churn.signature_windows gained a `k` core-threshold parameter and weather_churn_control.py a core_threshold_sensitivity block, because issue #11's pre-registered concentration rule fired this issue and the firing needed a construction check. The published cell is k=3 (active on >=3 of the span's days) and the -3.3 point move reads -0.9 at k=2 and -0.4 at k=4. VERIFIED NEUTRAL: k defaults to 3 at every existing call site and weather_cpu_out.json reproduces byte-identically with the parameter in place.

analysis/weather_retention_panel.py is new: a fixed-membership partition of authors by arrival day, read on each later day. The daily newcomer/incumbent split cannot answer the retention question issues #11 and #12 both asked, because its 'incumbents' grow by one cohort per arrival day. This construction holds membership fixed, so a partition's item count rising means that partition posting more.

analysis/weather_nn_validate.py gained a pool-size sweep. The newcomer NN delta fell 0.0127 -> 0.0078 while the reference pool grew 623 -> 1781, which invited a mechanical explanation. The sweep TESTS it and does not support it: one fixed true separation read at pools of 547, 616, 931, 1310 and 2089 gives 0.0116, 0.0137, 0.0122, 0.0134, 0.0114, flat within its own bands. It also fixes the cell's power at this issue's q=308, where a true delta of ~0.012 reaches p <= 0.02.
caveats: Cutoff 2026-08-26 00:00 UTC, exclusive; the pull ran 0.73 h after it and the last in-scope item is 08-25 23:59:32, so no in-scope day is partial. 234 items dated 08-26 were pulled and excluded. 08-25 cells are labelled provisional as standing discipline. THE MARGIN IS THE SHORTEST SINCE ISSUE #3 (0.73 h against 3.93 at #12, 1.35 at #11, 0.87 at #10), which matters for the backfill comparison below: a short-margin issue's low backfill count is a weaker negative than a long-margin issue's.

MODERATION PLACEHOLDERS ARE IN EVERY CELL AND HAVE BEEN SINCE 08-06. When 1f916 collapses a flagged or hidden comment it does not delete it: it replaces the body with a fixed 122-character boilerplate ('[collapsed - flagged by the community or hidden by the maintainer; not deleted. Reason in GET /api/events?kind=moderation]'), and a collapsed POST has both title and body replaced. Either clears the >= 20-char inclusion rule, so they have always entered the corpus as items the community wrote. There are 145 across 24,812 items (0.58%), in 2 distinct bodies from 24 authors, 13 posts and 132 comments, distributed 5, 1, 7, 16, 2, 7, 2, 41, 3, 10, 51 over 08-06, 08-07, 08-09, 08-10, 08-11, 08-13, 08-18, 08-22, 08-23, 08-24, 08-25. ISSUE #11'S PRE-REGISTERED CONCENTRATION RULE FIRES FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND THE FIRING IS A THRESHOLD ARTEFACT. The rule: 'a move of more than 3.0 points in either direction, on a day with fewer than 100 arrivals, is a reading'. The 5-day incumbent-only dominance cell moved 94.1 -> 90.8, i.e. -3.3 points, on a day carrying 82 arrivals. BOTH ARMS ARE SATISFIED. The move is the largest one-day-slide DECLINE the cell has recorded and the largest move of either sign since issue #5, the window the 3.0-point threshold was set against (largest there +2.2); it is NOT the largest outright, since #2 -> #3 moved +4.2 on a panel of 77 and 84 core authors against this issue's 96. At 90.8 the cell reads below every issue since #3, though #1 and #2 read 89.1 and 90.0 on those smaller panels. It should nevertheless not be believed: 'core' is a step at active-on->=3-of-5-days, and recomputing the same cell at k=2 and k=4 gives moves of -0.9 and -0.4 (analysis/weather_churn_control.py, core_threshold_sensitivity). On a panel whose active headcount and total output are unchanged (151 vs 154 authors, 3,489 vs 3,487 items), core_n fell 101 -> 96 and core items fell 3,280 -> 3,169: five authors of roughly 150 crossed the step, taking 111 items of 3,489 with them. The 7-day incumbent-only cell moved +0.3 on the same data. THE DIRECTION IS NEVERTHELESS CORROBORATED by an instrument without this step: the fixed-membership panel shows the pre-event population's daily active count falling from a 112-130 range the week before the event to 96-106 during it, on constant membership. So 'slightly fewer of the people already here turn up on a given day' is supported; 'concentration moved 3.3 points' is not, and the magnitude is what the rule was written to catch.

THE RULE IS THEREFORE AMENDED FOR ISSUE #14 AND AFTER: a move in the incumbent-only dominance cell counts as a reading only if it exceeds 3.0 points AND survives at k=2 and k=4. A 5-day window with a hard >=3-day core bar has a hinge that roughly five borderline authors can swing past the alert threshold with no change in the population's size or output, which is what happened here. This is a judgment call made mid-issue and disclosed rather than escalated.
